title: JudaismSourceGraph
description: Semantic Knowledge Relationship Graph for the Judaism Knowledge Base. Models conceptual, historical, textual, and polemical relationships among Jewish texts, authorities, traditions, movements, and themes. Architecturally distinguished from runtime execution/dependency graphs (which enforce strict DAG with 0 cycles for scheduling and activation). In this semantic knowledge graph, dialectical/discursive relationships (reciprocal pairs such as CHALLENGES and RESPONDS_TO) are valid representations of historical debate (e.g. Saadia Gaon vs. Karaism), while structural lineage and historical precedence edges (DERIVES_FROM, PART_OF, BELONGS_TO, HISTORICALLY_PRECEDES) remain strictly acyclic.

metadata.description: Graph metadata specifying topological semantics, classification, and validation rules.

execution_dependency_dag.description: False for semantic knowledge graph; runtime execution graph remains strict DAG with 0 cycles.

lineage_subgraph_dag.description: True: hierarchical and lineage edges (DERIVES_FROM, PART_OF, BELONGS_TO, HISTORICALLY_PRECEDES) must form a strict DAG with 0 cycles.

permits_reciprocal_dialogue.description: True: reciprocal dialectical pairs (e.g. CHALLENGES <-> RESPONDS_TO) are valid representations of historical debates.

relationship.description: Semantic relationship connecting nodes. Edge categories: (1) Lineage/Hierarchical: DERIVES_FROM, PART_OF, BELONGS_TO, HISTORICALLY_PRECEDES (strict DAG required); (2) Epistemic/Evidentiary: SUPPORTS, INTERPRETS, QUOTES, SUMMARIZES; (3) Dialectical/Discursive: CHALLENGES, RESPONDS_TO, CONTRADICTS (permits reciprocal dialogical pairs between debate interlocutors).
